web_blocks.html: 8.1 Stage 3 vs. Stage 2 Reclaim Reconciliation & Moving Averages

After falling 26.54% from its $603.88 peak to a $328.57 low, ISRG closed on November 13, 2026 at $443.59 (+0.84% 1D, -2.93% 1W, +4.42% 1M, +10.62% 3M) [23]. Our technical signals split across timeframes and require explicit reconciliation. The automated stock_snapshot.py screen flags a short-term Stage 2 reclaim because price sits +8.46% above the 30-week SMA ($409.00) and +4.45% above the 10-week EMA ($424.71), inside an 11.15% Bollinger squeeze [23]. However, our primary ledger (facts_US_2026-11-13.json) classifies ISRG as Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback). Why? The 200-day SMA ($429.38) is still declining from $476.17 sixty-three trading days ago, the 50-day SMA ($417.59) remains below the 200-day SMA ($429.38), ISRG logged 7 distribution days in the last 25 sessions, and the S&P 500 sits in a Correction regime [23].

We defer to the primary ledger's Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback) classification and set our posture to WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT. On the 4-hour chart, ISRG coils on its 50-period SMA ($443.03) and below its 20-period EMA ($448.95), with 4H RSI(14) at 47.50, daily RSI(14) at 52.08, and weekly RSI(14) at 55.60 [23]. Average True Range (ATR 14) is $14.45 (3.26% of CMP) [23]. Until the 200-day SMA flattens or turns up and price breaks out above Pivot R1 ($464.22) on volume—or successfully tests and holds the $418.34–$431.08 support zone—chasing $443.59 is premature. Hard invalidation sits at $401.77 [23].

web_blocks.html: 8.2 Volume Contraction, Institutional Flow & Short Interest

Volume confirms quiet institutional buying rather than selling [22, 23]. On November 13, 2026, ISRG traded 1.60 million shares—just 0.65x its 30-day average of 2.47 million shares (and 0.68x Finviz relative volume) [22, 23]. Drying volume inside an 11.15% Bollinger squeeze is textbook Volatility Contraction Pattern (VCP) action, showing post-Q3 supply is absorbed. Institutions own 90.64% of shares (-0.44% recent net change), insiders hold 0.70% (-2.51% routine Form 4 sales), and short interest is low at 2.05% of float (7.06 million shares, 2.98 days to cover) [22]. In addition, management bought back $2.94 billion of stock in Q3 2026 alone, placing a strong corporate bid under the shares [3].

For defined-risk upside once support or breakout confirms, our options desk flags the 2027-09-17 $400 LEAPS Call (306 DTE, 0.71 Delta) under an IV_FAIR regime [27]. ATM implied volatility is 46.5% versus 20-day realized volatility of 44.6% [27]. However, two hard execution constraints apply. First, liquidity is thin: open interest is just 7 contracts with an $8.00 bid-ask spread ($89.00 bid / $97.00 ask), creating roughly 4%+ slippage risk at the $93.00 midpoint—use strict limit orders only [27]. Second, the $9,300.00 debit (930.0 bps of a $100,000 reference NAV) exceeds our actual $7,434.75 consolidated cash ($88,684.68 net worth), requiring fresh cash or trimming an existing holding. Expiration breakeven is $493.00 (+11.14% vs CMP); if filled on a support hold, trim half at +75%–100% gain and exit on a weekly close below $429.38 [27].

book_subsections.title: Reconciling Stage 3 vs. Stage 2: Why Patience Beats Chasing $443.59
paragraphs: A great business bought at the wrong point in its technical cycle can tie up capital for quarters. After peaking at $603.88 and sliding to $328.57, ISRG closed on November 13, 2026 at $443.59. On the surface, our automated stock_snapshot.py screen flags an early Stage 2 reclaim: price sits 8.46 percent above the 30-week SMA ($409.00) and 4.45 percent above the 10-week EMA ($424.71) inside an 11.15 percent Bollinger squeeze.

However, our primary facts ledger classifies ISRG as Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback), and for good reason. The 200-day SMA ($429.38) is still declining from $476.17 sixty-three trading days ago, the 50-day SMA ($417.59) sits below the 200-day SMA ($429.38), the stock logged 7 distribution days in 25 sessions, and the S&P 500 is in a Correction regime. Even though four-hour RSI (47.50) and daily RSI (52.08) show no overbought froth, buying into overhead distribution before the 200-day average flattens creates unnecessary drawdown risk.

Accordingly, we honor the primary Stage 3 classification and wait for confirmation. We want to see either a decisive volume breakout above Pivot R1 ($464.22) alongside a flattening 200-day SMA, or a disciplined pullback that holds the $418.34 to $431.08 support zone above our $401.77 hard stop.

book_subsections.title: Stock Replacement with Defined Risk: Liquidity & Cash Constraints
paragraphs: For investors who prefer defined-risk convexity once support holds, the September 17, 2027 $400 Call (306 DTE, 0.71 Delta) trades near $93.00 per share ($9,300.00 debit) under an IV Fair regime (46.5% ATM IV vs. 44.6% HV20). Max loss is capped at $9,300.00 with a $493.00 expiration breakeven, and a weekly close below $429.38 limits early-stop loss to roughly $448 (-4.8%).

Two practical constraints govern execution. First, open interest is just 7 contracts with an $8.00 bid-ask spread ($89.00 bid / $97.00 ask), creating roughly 4%+ slippage risk—making strict limit orders near the $93.00 midpoint mandatory. Second, the $9,300.00 debit (930.0 bps of a $100,000 reference NAV) exceeds our actual $7,434.75 consolidated cash ($88,684.68 net worth), meaning this contract cannot be funded without fresh cash or trimming an existing holding.

Even with those constraints, understanding the LEAPS payoff profile is useful once ISRG confirms support. At $510.13 to $515.00, the $400 Call is modeled to gain roughly $3,982 (+42.8% on risk), and at our $586.65 to $590.00 Bull Target it gains roughly $10,786 (+116.0%). Daily theta decay is modest at $13.50 per day across 306 days to expiration. Still, options leverage magnifies poor timing: buying an illiquid LEAPS contract during Stage 3 distribution before support holds invites immediate mark-to-market slippage, so patience comes first.

book_subsections.title: Moving-Average Architecture, Support Geometry, and Execution Rules
paragraphs: Let us walk through the exact price levels on the chart so execution remains mechanical. At $443.59, ISRG sits below its 20-day SMA ($447.13), 4-hour 20-EMA ($448.95), and Pivot R1 ($464.22). A daily close above $464.22 on at least 1.3 times the 30-day average volume (2.47 million shares) alongside a flattening 200-day SMA would confirm upward resolution toward R2 ($496.44) and our $515.00 Base Target.

On the downside, our $418.34 to $431.08 support zone brackets the 200-day SMA ($429.38), 10-week EMA ($424.71), and 50-day SMA ($417.59), with the 30-week SMA ($409.00) and Pivot S1 ($394.45) below. Placing the hard stop at $401.77 keeps risk bounded if Stage 3 rollover resumes, while waiting for $418.34–$431.08 support lifts reward-to-risk to 2.86:1–5.83:1.

Volume and ownership data also explain why a patient limit bid works well here. Institutions hold 90.64 percent of ISRG shares, short interest is low at 2.05 percent of float (2.98 days to cover), and management retired $2.94 billion of stock in Q3 2026. On November 13, 2026, daily volume of 1.60 million shares was 0.65 times the 30-day average of 2.47 million. That dry-up shows sellers are not panicking, yet 7 distribution days over the past 25 sessions confirm that overhead supply still needs time to clear. Meanwhile, ISRG's 10.62 percent three-month gain (+13.64 percent over 63 trading days) shows relative strength against a weak S&P 500, making $418.34–$431.08 a high-probability area to monitor.
